finding: Euro-area sovereign fragmentation intensified: France-Germany 10Y spread widened to ~150bp, highest since the 2011 sovereign-debt crisis, with selling signs spreading to Italy and Greece while EUR remains under pressure.
net_new_delta: Prior state identified French fragmentation near 140bp; fresh evidence shows widening to ~150bp plus cross-sovereign contagion signs, elevating the hypothesis from France-specific fiscal repricing toward euro-area fragmentation risk.

evidence.claim: French-German 10Y spread widened to about 150bp, highest since the euro-area sovereign debt crisis in 2011; selling showed signs of spreading to Italy and Greece; EUR on track for fourth weekly fall.
ECB policymaker Nagel said ECB tools safeguard price stability rather than target specific sovereign spread levels.

conflicts: US Treasury yields and oil eased into Oct 2, so euro-area spread widening is not fully explained by a contemporaneous global duration or oil upswing.
Italy and Greece have improved fiscal trajectories, yet Reuters reports selling signs spreading to them.
unknown: Persistence and depth of contagion are unproven.
No evidence establishes market dysfunction, forced selling, or imminent ECB intervention.
next_decisive_check: Test whether OAT-Bund remains near/above 150bp and BTP/Greek spreads continue widening after US payrolls, especially if US yields and Brent remain softer.

oracle.finding: Upgrade the research state from France-specific fiscal stress to a falsifiable euro-area fragmentation/contagion hypothesis; condition EUR and European-equity models on cross-sovereign spread breadth, not OAT-Bund alone.

supermesh_x.finding: Fresh Reuters evidence separates European sovereign-spread contagion from easing US yields/oil; preserve OAT-Bund, BTP-Bund and Greek spread breadth as distinct provenance channels and do not infer liquidity dysfunction without direct evidence.
